about: workflow:keep-my-search-index-beside-a-copy-of-my-results: keeps the person's search index of their own results in the person's store, fed by small pages of what changed so a save never waits on it, with a clean-up walk in key order. It replaces tools/keep-my-search-index-beside-a-copy-of-my-results/from-an-older-version/src/search-cleanup-pages.mjs, whose whole job was paging the index rows of a table through the old store's SQL (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep my search index beside a copy of my results
payload.job: Keep a search index of the person's own results in the person's own store, fed by small pages of what changed, so a save never waits on the index; a clean-up walk pages through the index in key order.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for results, their change list and the word index, proven on the example attempts, and each save, page, search and clean-up page kept, read back or refused.

source.from: tools/keep-my-search-index-beside-a-copy-of-my-results/from-an-older-version/src/search-cleanup-pages.mjs (SQL paging over a table with a cursor and a page of 1 to 128 rows, from the old tree), read on the Workshop origin/main 13c05f2c8c
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job: a result, its change, the index rows made from it and the clean-up walk over them. The SQL text, the rowid and the table name were the old store's own form and are not carried; the store makes its own objects in its own language. A word search is the store's own query.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the index is kept, when it already is

operations.description: Operations to run this time, each one of save {id, text}, delete {id}, index_page {limit}, search {word} or clean_page {limit, cursor}

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the index is already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep it.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: results (id, text, when it was saved), a change list in the order the changes were made (one change for each save or delete, with the result's id and a sequence number), the index (for each indexed result, its words, so a word finds the results that hold it), the set of indexed results, and one cursor for the index pages and one for the clean-up walk. A save writes the result and its change in one write and never reads the index, so it does not wait on it. An index page takes at most limit changes (1 to 128) after its cursor, in sequence order: a result that is still there is indexed again with its words, a result that is gone is taken out of the index; then the cursor moves on. A clean-up page takes at most limit indexed results with an id after the cursor, in id order, and says whether more follow. Refuse a limit outside 1 to 128, and an id or word that is empty. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, run these operations in order, each through the store's own objects: [{"op": "save", "id": "r1", "text": "bakery bread sourdough"}, {"op": "save", "id": "r2", "text": "bakery cake lemon"}, {"op": "save", "id": "r3", "text": "garden tomatoes"}, {"op": "index_page", "limit": 2}, {"op": "index_page", "limit": 2}, {"op": "search", "word": "bakery"}, {"op": "save", "id": "r2", "text": "bakery cake orange"}, {"op": "delete", "id": "r3"}, {"op": "index_page", "limit": 128}, {"op": "search", "word": "tomatoes"}, {"op": "search", "word": "orange"}, {"op": "clean_page", "limit": 1, "cursor": null}, {"op": "clean_page", "limit": 1, "cursor": "r1"}, {"op": "index_page", "limit": 0}]. Answers: save and delete give saved and deleted; index_page gives {indexed, more} with the ids it indexed or took out, in order; search gives the ids of the indexed results holding the word, in id order; clean_page gives {rows, more} with the ids after the cursor; an operation that is refused gives refused. Then remove the throwaway place. Submit answers: one answer per attempt, in order, exactly as the answers above.

checks.says: Each attempt gives the answer the intent says

steps.title: Keep this run's operations
steps.do: Run each item of operations through the store's own objects, in order, and read back every result it saved or took out and every indexed result. With no operations, submit empty lists. Submit answers (one per operation, as in the prove step), and found_results (each result read back, by id, with whether it is indexed).

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes every result, its change list and its index rows; a result the person deletes is taken out of the index by the next index page.
